A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
N. tricholoma recruitment can be prevented if native perennial grasses are present in the sward at >0.5 DM/ha, or if the sward is grazed to maintain >2 t DM/ ha and 100% cover.
the best management option to prevent establishment of N. trichtoma is to maintain >2 t DM/ ha and 100% perennial grass ground cover, and to avoid grazing during the summer period.
N. trichocotoma seedling invasion can be prevented in pastures with >0.5 kg DM/m2, which can be achieved through rotational grazing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the level of perennial grass competition required to prevent recruitment of N. trichotoma seed is relatively small, and that the timing of this competition is critical.
the presence of a substantial amount of native perennial grass (>1 t DM/ ha measured in spring) and rotational grazing can be used to reduce the establishment of N. tricho-toma.
N. tricholoma seedling recruitment is a major component of its invasion process and can be controlled by maintaining sufficient groundcover and DM production in the native perennial grass swards.
